clue.text: Throat trouble arises when coating of pills is removed

indicators.note: is removed tells us to take letters away from the phrase meaning arises

parts.note: something that arises crops up

indicators.note: the coating of something is its outside, so the first and last letters of pills

explanation.surface: A sore throat develops after the sugar shell of some tablets is taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arises' gives the phrase CROPS UP; 'coating of pills' gives P and S, and 'is removed' takes those out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Croup is a childhood infection of the windpipe and larynx giving a barking cough.

clue.text: PA's a treasure, returning call

definitions.note: PA is a public-address system; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: returning means the word for treasure is read backwards

parts.note: a gem is a treasure, a precious thing
to call someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: Dad is a real gem, giving a ring back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PA' looks like Father but is a public-address system; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loudhailer is a simple public-address device for amplifying a voice.

clue.text: Vehicle insurance giving universal protection here in Canada

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: insurance cover giving protection wraps around the letter for universal

parts.note: insurance is cover
U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A motor policy that covers you anywhere is available in this Canadian place.
explanation.definitionFit: Vancouver is a major city on Canada's Pacific coast, the place indicated.

clue.text: To stay at the crease, this mustn't be dropped by team

definitions.meaning: in cricket a batsman who stays in carries on batting, two words joined

definitions.text: this mustn't be dropped by team
definitions.meaning: a relay team passes a stick between runners and loses if it falls

explanation.walkthrough: The crease is where a cricket batsman stands; staying there means continuing to bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Batting on describes staying in at cricket, and a relay runner's stick is the second sense.

clue.text: Grubs from river put in can — water oddly lacking

indicators.note: put in places the river abbreviation inside the word for can

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet, as is lav
R is the map abbreviation for river

indicators.note: lacking its odd letters, so only the second and fourth letters of water remain

explanation.surface: Insect young taken from a stream are placed in a tin without much water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' is the British slang for a toilet here, not a tin; 'oddly lacking' keeps only the even letters of 'water'.
explanation.definitionFit: Larvae are the young grub stage of insects before pupation.

clue.text: What the gambler'll do, seizing note with reckless intent

indicators.note: seizing means the gambler's phrase grabs and holds the note inside it

parts.note: a gambler will bet, so 'he'll bet'

explanation.surface: A punter grabs a banknote, determined to throw it away recklessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What the gambler'll do' is HE'LL BET; N goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell-bent means recklessly determined to do something regardless of consequences.

clue.text: Validate words of constraint at end of session

indicators.note: at end of places the word for constraint after the word for session

parts.note: a spell is a period or session of activity
a check is a restraint or constraint

explanation.surface: Restraining phrases are imposed when a meeting closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Words of constraint' looks like a magic spell, but 'Validate words' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spellcheck verifies that written words are correctly spelt.

clue.text: When called out, fix part of window frame

indicators.note: when called out means spoken, so we want a word sounding like fix

parts.note: a jam is a fix, a tight spot

explanation.surface: Shouting, someone repairs a section of window frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is a vertical side post of a door or window frame.

clue.text: Power within grasp of outstanding kid

indicators.note: within grasp of means held inside the word for outstanding

parts.note: an outstanding bill is due
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A brilliant child holds power in their hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' is the verb, to fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid someone is to deceive or fool them, a verb sense of the answer.

clue.text: Agent carrying explosive fuel lit with malice

indicators.note: carrying means the agent holds the scrambled letters inside

parts.note: an agent is a spy

indicators.note: explosive suggests the letters of fuel and lit are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A secret agent with a fuel bomb sets it off with evil intent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive' rearranges the letters of 'fuel lit' (to ITEFULL), and 'carrying' puts them inside the agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting spitefully means acting out of malice or a desire to hurt.

clue.text: Team with money from Brazil, dependant on stars

parts.note: a side is a sports team
the real is the currency of Brazil

explanation.surface: A football club funded with Brazilian cash relies on its star players.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal means relating to or determined by the stars, as in sidereal time.

clue.text: One step described by senior astronaut

indicators.note: described by means drawn around, so the senior abbreviation encloses the step

parts.note: a pace is one step

explanation.surface: An elderly spaceman recounts taking a single step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Described' in its geometric sense means drawn round.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacer is a rarer informal word for someone who travels in space.

clue.text: Unconventional attire a Cricket Club initially rejected

indicators.note: rejected means those letters are thrown out of the word for attire

parts.note: to accoutre is to attire or equip

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of a, Cricket and Club

explanation.surface: Odd clothing was turned down by a sports club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attire' is the verb, ACCOUTRE; the initials ACC are dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means unusual and startlingly unconventional, a French borrowing.

clue.text: Location marker on map to indulge criminal?

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is it a crime on a map to give in to oneself?
explanation.definitionFit: Longitude, measured east or west of Greenwich, fixes a position on a map.

clue.text: Nutritious food as chopped in chop

indicators.note: in places the word as and the word for chopped inside the word for chop

parts.note: to chop is to cut
chopped wood is hewn

explanation.surface: A healthy dish where something is cut up inside a cutlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopped' and 'chop' look like one repeated idea, but one is the past tense meaning hewn and the other the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashew nuts are an edible, protein-rich kernel eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Worked half-heartedly with protective cover

indicators.note: half-heartedly removes one of the letters at the heart of the word

parts.note: to work hard is to toil, so worked is toiled

explanation.surface: Someone laboured listlessly under shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: TOILED has the heart OI; losing half of it, the O, leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiled roof or floor is covered with tiles, which protect it.

clue.text: Cultivated French lilies in cape covered with greenery

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape

indicators.note: in means the French lilies sit inside the word for overgrown

parts.note: ivied means covered with ivy
lis is French for lilies, as in fleur-de-lis

explanation.surface: Lilies grown on a headland overgrown with plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivated' looks like gardening but means refined.
explanation.definitionFit: Cultivated people are refined and cultured, as are civilised ones.

clue.text: One who has wife enters divorce centre from the rear

indicators.note: enters means the wife letter goes inside
from the rear means the divorce centre is read backwards

parts.note: Reno in Nevada was famous for quick divorces

explanation.surface: A married man walks into a divorce office by the back door.
explanation.walkthrough: RENO, the Nevada city famous for quick divorces, reversed is ONER, with W inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is a person who possesses something.

clue.text: Most likely learner in pet project headed by master

indicators.note: headed by puts the word for master at the front in this down clue

parts.note: a pro is a master of a craft

indicators.note: in places the learner letter inside the pet project

parts.note: a pet project is one's baby
L is the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: A trainee joins a cherished scheme led by an expert, probably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headed by' puts the master first, as the answer is written downwards; 'in' places the learner inside one's pet scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Probably means in all likelihood, the most likely outcome.

clue.text: Suggest I should be kept out of the picture

indicators.note: kept out of means the letter I is removed from the word for the picture

parts.note: a picture is a film, a movie

explanation.surface: Someone proposes that they themselves be excluded from the photo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The picture' is a film, MOVIE; drop the I.
explanation.definitionFit: To move a motion is to propose or suggest it formally in a meeting.

clue.text: Dicey grant messed up urban development

indicators.note: messed up means the letters of dicey grant are jumbled

explanation.surface: A risky subsidy botched a town-planning project.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden city is a planned town with green spaces, such as Letchworth in England.

clue.text: Folk preferring books to work, often seen on beach

indicators.note: preferring books to work means the books replace the work

parts.note: folk are people
OP is short for opus, a work
BB is an abbreviation for books

explanation.surface: Bookish types who'd rather read than work go to the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: In PEOPLE the OP (work) is replaced by BB (books).
explanation.definitionFit: A pebble is a small smooth stone typically found on a shore.

clue.text: Half of 12 with 10, unusually alert

indicators.note: unusually means the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: the first half of the answer at 12 across
the answer at 10 across

explanation.surface: Combine two answers and the result is surprisingly watchful.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 across is HELL-BENT; its first half, HELL, with BATON (10 across) is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the ball means being quick and alert, an idiom.

clue.text: This drawer's restricted by modern standards

indicators.note: restricted by means the letters are confined within the words modern standards

explanation.surface: An artist is limited by contemporary norms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' is one who draws, the surrealist artist Max Ernst, not furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German surrealist painter and artist.

clue.text: Melancholy report of Adam's transgression?

definitions.meaning: Adam is the first man, a chap; his sin was the Fall, so a headline reads that a chap has fallen

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a fanciful reading: CHAP (Adam) and FALLEN (his transgression in Eden).
explanation.definitionFit: Chapfallen means dispirited, with the jaw hanging down in dejection.

clue.text: Dispatches page with revision accepted by old partners

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside the old partners

parts.note: exes are former partners
an edit is a revision

explanation.surface: A page with corrections is taken on by former partners and sent off.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite is to send off or deal with promptly, as one dispatches business.

clue.text: Steady broadcast of Derby info

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Constant coverage of the horse race at Epsom.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a famous English horse race at Epsom. 'Steady' is the noun, a regular partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady is a regular romantic partner, such as a boyfriend.

clue.text: Cancelled run, short of initial copy

parts.note: a cancelled event is off

indicators.note: short of initial means lacking its first letter

parts.note: a sprint is a run

explanation.surface: A print run was cancelled, with no first copy produced.
explanation.definitionFit: An offprint is a separately printed copy of an article from a journal.

clue.text: Current duo starting broadcast recalled Cooke's last Letter from America

indicators.note: the first two letters starting the word broadcast
recalled means read backwards
last takes the final letter of Cooke's

parts.note: Americans call the letter Z zee

explanation.surface: Two people beginning a broadcast remember Alistair Cooke's final radio talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Letter from America was Alistair Cooke's long-running BBC radio talk. 'Recalled' turns the E and the American letter name round, giving EEZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is a light current of air.

clue.text: I invested in fund showing ultimate loss, but I'll bear it

indicators.note: invested in means put inside the fund
ultimate loss means the last letter is lost

parts.note: a stock is a fund or supply

explanation.surface: An investor puts money in a falling fund, accepting the loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic endures hardship without complaint, saying so of their trouble.

clue.text: Caught on pitch, he's far from gracious

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to pitch is to throw, or hurl

explanation.surface: A rude cricketer is taken out on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like the playing field but is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A churl is a rude, ill-mannered and boorish person.

clue.text: What Aran workers may do to fuse?

definitions.meaning: Aran jumpers are hand-made with needles and wool
join together, as broken bones do

explanation.walkthrough: Aran is a cable-patterned woollen jumper from the Aran Islands of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken bones knit when they join together, as things fuse.
